items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 6:1
items.html: The vessels, which are the expansion of reflected light from the screen and Malchut of the Rosh [head] downward, are discerned as coarseness even before their expansion into the Guf [body]; but they are not discernible before the light has departed from within them, as above in Item 71. And when the light departed from within them, then the coarseness that had been in them while they were still in Malchut of the Rosh was recognised, and also the additional coarseness that they have now newly acquired — namely, that they remained in darkness without light, which is a discernment of judgement and a coarseness that was not in them before they expanded into the Guf. (Chapter 6, Item 3)
